objective: Proof. Assemble A, B and C: parity's count is polynomial, the not-exactly-two and twelve classes have coNP-complete failures, and not-all-equal never fails; so, unless NP-complete problems are polynomial, no value-free four-place knot is mutually selecting on 4-regular systems. Together with B for every k >= 4, the value-free not-all-equal law fails on regular systems only at three places. State what remains open (laws that prefer a value; counting).
status: Proved by FOUR-PLACE-20261031-001D-P001: unless NP-complete problems are polynomial, no value-free four-place knot is mutually selecting on 4-regular systems (parity's count is 2^(n-r) or 0; not-exactly-two and twelve have coNP-complete failures; not-all-equal never fails); with B, value-free not-all-equal fails on regular systems only at three places (the knot's Pfaffian spaces), so mutual selection among value-free laws is special to three places
title: No value-free four-place law has mutual selection
